senses.en: the process of making air, water or land dirty and dangerous, or the substances that do this
examples: Air **pollution** in the city is getting worse.
Factories are a major cause of water **pollution**.
We must reduce **pollution** from traffic.

forms.en: to make air, water or land dirty and unsafe
forms.ex: The factory **polluted** the river for years.

pollution.note: **Uncountable** — never *pollutions*. Say *a lot of pollution* or *high levels of pollution*.

senses.en: the cutting down of forests over a large area
examples: **Deforestation** destroys the habitat of many species.
**Deforestation** is a major cause of flooding.
The government has promised to slow **deforestation**.

senses.en: at risk of disappearing completely, especially a kind of animal or plant
examples: The Saola is an **endangered** species.
Many **endangered** animals live in this park.
Tigers became **endangered** through hunting.

forms.en: to put someone or something at risk

endangered.note: **Extinct** is the next stage: an *endangered* species still exists; an *extinct* one is gone.

senses.en: the natural place where a plant or animal normally lives
examples: The forest is the **habitat** of many rare birds.
Building roads destroys natural **habitats**.
This frog's **habitat** is the mountain stream.

habitat.note: A **habitat** belongs to an animal or plant. The wider surroundings we all share is the *environment*.

senses.en: a group of animals or plants of the same kind that can breed together
examples: This **species** is found only in Viet Nam.
Hundreds of **species** are lost every year.
Scientists discovered a new **species** of frog.

species.note: The plural is also **species** — never *specie* or *specieses*. *One species, two species.*

senses.en: the protection of the natural world, or the careful use of something so it is not wasted
senses.vi: sự bảo tồn, bảo vệ (thiên nhiên)
examples: She works in wildlife **conservation**.
**Conservation** of water matters most in the dry season.
The park was set up for the **conservation** of rare plants.

forms.en: to use something carefully so it is not wasted, or to protect nature
forms.ex: Turn off the tap to **conserve** water.

senses.en: waste paper, cans and other rubbish left lying in a public place
examples: There was **litter** all over the beach.
Please don't drop **litter** in the park.
Volunteers collected three bags of **litter**.

senses.en: to leave rubbish lying in a public place
examples: People who **litter** can be fined.
The path was **littered** with plastic bottles.

litter.note: **Uncountable** — never *litters*. *Litter* is rubbish in the wrong place; *rubbish* (BrE) / *garbage* (AmE) is waste in general.

senses.en: to treat used materials so that they can be made into something new
examples: We **recycle** paper, glass and plastic at home.
These bags are made from **recycled** bottles.
Only a small part of our waste is **recycled**.

recycle.note: One of the three Rs: **reduce**, **reuse**, **recycle** — in that order of usefulness.

senses.en: to make something smaller in size, amount or number
examples: We should **reduce** the amount of plastic we use.
Cycling to school **reduces** pollution.
The shop has **reduced** its prices.

forms.en: the act of making something smaller
forms.ex: There has been a **reduction** in litter.

reduce.note: Opposite: *increase*. Stress the second syllable: re-**DUCE**.

senses.en: to use something again instead of throwing it away
examples: **Reuse** your water bottle instead of buying a new one.
These jars can be **reused** for storage.
We **reuse** the paper by printing on both sides.

reuse.note: **Reuse** means use again as it is; **recycle** means break it down and make something new. The verb is /ˌriːˈjuːz/ with a /z/; the noun *reuse* ends in /s/.

senses.en: waste water and human waste carried away in pipes
examples: Untreated **sewage** was flowing into the river.
The town is building a new **sewage** treatment plant.
**Sewage** must be cleaned before it reaches the sea.

senses.en: a chemical used to kill insects and other pests that damage crops
examples: Too much **pesticide** contaminates the soil.
**Pesticides** can harm bees as well as pests.
The farm has stopped using chemical **pesticides**.

senses.en: to make something dirty, polluted or poisonous by adding a harmful substance
senses.vi: làm nhiễm bẩn, làm ô nhiễm
examples: Chemicals from the factory **contaminated** the water.
The soil has been **contaminated** by pesticides.
Don't let the raw meat **contaminate** the vegetables.

forms.en: the state of being made impure or poisonous

senses.en: to keep someone or something safe from harm or damage
examples: We must **protect** the environment for future generations.
The park **protects** several rare species.
Sunscreen **protects** your skin **from** the sun.

forms.en: the act of keeping something safe

senses.en: to keep something in its original state so that it is not lost or damaged
examples: National parks **preserve** natural habitats.
We must **preserve** these forests for the future.
The wetlands have been carefully **preserved**.

senses.en: a large area of countryside protected by the government for its nature and beauty
examples: Cuc Phuong is Viet Nam's oldest **national park**.
Hunting is forbidden inside the **national park**.
We camped in the **national park** for two nights.

senses.en: animals and plants that live and grow in natural conditions
examples: The park is home to rare **wildlife**.
Pollution threatens **wildlife** in the river.
She photographs **wildlife** for a living.

wildlife.note: **Uncountable** and written as one word — never *wildlifes*.

senses.en: knowing that something exists and being interested in it
examples: The campaign raised **awareness of** plastic waste.
There is growing **awareness** of climate change.
The poster aims to increase public **awareness**.

forms.en: knowing that something exists or is true
forms.ex: Are you **aware** of the new rules?

awareness.note: The usual verb is **raise** awareness, not *make* or *rise*.
